title: Rank improvement turns by recurring cause; show Athena-own dispatch
summary: Follow-up to job 20261110-181101-xs11 (queued, never verified, no candidate): the improvement turn in Plan::build_improving now picks the ready Athena-own request whose cause is recorded in the most distinct jobs (hestia::improvement_of counts), newest first, instead of by plan rank. `athena plan` prints each Athena-own request's expected dispatch number. The one-in-three share stays unchanged. The audience is the person running Athena and the steward, who need steward fixes to run soon.

defaults_applied.how: Tests for the new ranking and the plan output, with cargo test and clippy passing.
Criteria check the 6 newer items taking the first improvement turns, not that code exists.
One focused change to plan.rs, the plan display and the changelog.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (Improvement, ImprovementTurn, IMPROVEMENT_GAP, Plan::build_improving; the turn walk picks the first ready improvement item in plan order, i.e. by priority, rung, age), crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (improvement_of fills Improvement.cause_jobs) and crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (plan() prints `turn` lines only for items that took a turn). No record or data file is added, so no records validation or AnyRecord change.

Recorded finding on job 20261110-181101-xs11: the current rule takes ready Athena-own requests by plan order (priority, rung, then oldest first), which is the by-age case the request says to replace. The change keeps that job's intent and files (plan.rs, CHANGELOG.md) and adds display.rs because `athena plan` output is built there; no prior candidate exists, so no earlier work is kept or dropped.
Newest first means descending request id, as ids begin with a timestamp. Ties in cause count fall to newest. An item with no cause_jobs entry counts as 0.
Expected dispatch number of an Athena-own request is its 1-based place in the final Plan::order (after turn moves), the same numbering the existing `turn` lines use.
Readiness rules (dependencies, tried items, skipped unreadable requests) and the urgent promotion at REPEAT_URGENT_JOBS stay as they are; only the choice among ready candidates changes.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need no change.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs builds 200 older ordinary items, 10 older Athena-own items and 6 newer Athena-own items with higher cause_jobs counts; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes and the test asserts the 6 newer items take the first 6 improvement turns (dispatches 3, 6, 9, ...).
A unit test in plan.rs shows that among ready Athena-own requests with equal cause_jobs counts, the newest id takes the turn first; `cargo test -p athena-core` passes.
The existing improvement_turn tests in plan.rs still pass (or are updated only where they relied on age order), and the diff leaves IMPROVEMENT_GAP at 2 (`git diff` shows no change to that constant).
A test in crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs shows `plan()` output containing a line with each Athena-own request's id and its expected dispatch number; `cargo test -p athena-cli` passes.
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has a new entry describing the new improvement-turn ranking (distinct jobs of the cause, then newest) and the dispatch numbers in `athena plan`.
The doc comment of Plan::build_improving in plan.rs describes the new choice rule, replacing the 'best ranked' wording.

out_of_scope: The one-in-three share (IMPROVEMENT_GAP) and the rule for when a turn is due
The reserved fix lane, daily-dispatch cap, wait-time warnings and the stale-request review from the introspection's proposed request
Retiring, reordering or editing existing queued requests or any records/ files
athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows and other governance files
departures: Slightly higher cost than the reference: a ranking change in a large file plus display work and test setup with 216 items.
hard_reason: It changes the run pipeline's dispatch order: which queued request is dispatched on each improvement turn.
